evidence: Receiving P assay 48 h = 3.10 g/L (available 52 h), consistent with sources at 48 h: 3.06, 3.02, 2.98 g/L
Source peaks 72-76 h: 8.36, 8.21, 8.02 g/L, then decline to ~6.4-7.0 by 96 h
Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 10.84 mg/L; sources' minimum DO2 over 72-96 h ~7.4-8.1 mg/L, well above 2.0 mg/L constraint
Receiving DO2 trend (48-52 h, ~11.0-10.8 mg/L) matches source trajectories over same window
submission.rationale: At the 52 h decision point the receiving fermentation is on the source trajectory: P(48 h) = 3.10 g/L vs sources 3.0/3.0/3.0 g/L, and DO2 (~10.8 mg/L) matches the source pattern with ample margin above the 2 mg/L minimum. Source batches show the run is just entering its main production phase, peaking ~8.1-8.4 g/L near 72-76 h with DO2 never dropping below ~7.4 mg/L. Feed reduction or aeration changes would cut productive growth or waste capacity with no evidenced oxygen risk. The historically observed dip near 24-28 h and recovery already occurred identically in the receiving batch. KEEP preserves product mass and lets the batch reach its natural peak; harvesting around 72-76 h (a scheduling note, not an action here) would capture the maximum.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters may differ from the sources; if the receiving batch lags or DO2 drops faster than the sources after 52 h, an aeration increase could become relevant. The next routine assay (56 h availability) will confirm trajectory; DO2 is monitored online so any oxygen-constraint risk would be visible in time to intervene at a later review.
